implementation_notes: Vitest (like Jest) implements the whole loop for TypeScript projects: toMatchSnapshot stores a pretty-printed reference under __snapshots__/ and compares on later runs, -u/--update re-records, CI mode refuses to write and fails on missing or obsolete snapshots, and toMatchFileSnapshot compares against an explicit file path so whole-file artefacts (generated code, reports, HTML) keep their extension and syntax highlighting. That replaces the hand-written recorder/comparator; typed fixtures or zod-style parsers can narrow what is captured before it is serialized, which keeps the reference small and stable. The classic hand-rolled form is only needed when the artefact is produced outside the test process and no framework-managed store is wanted.
pitfalls: Generic snapshots escape quotes and backticks and lose syntax highlighting; use toMatchFileSnapshot for readable output and never point it at a path Vitest manages (such as __snapshots__/x.snap).
Async concurrent tests must take expect from the test context, otherwise assertions are attributed to the wrong test and snapshots land under unexpected names.
Obsolete snapshots survive deleted tests and still count as coverage; treat the obsolete-snapshot failure as work to do rather than noise to silence.

variants.name: Inline snapshots in the test source
variants.implementation_notes: toMatchInlineSnapshot() keeps the reference in the test file and rewrites the call with the recorded value (delegating formatting to prettier when configured). It is the right form for compact values that belong in the review diff next to the assertion; large multi-line artefacts should use a file snapshot instead, where the reference can be diffed as its own file.
pitfalls: Inline snapshots write to source files, so a read-only CI checkout must run with updates disabled (default in CI mode).
Prettier/formatting settings alter how the literal is written, producing churn unrelated to behaviour.
